response.text:
Evidence supports the shortcut concern, but I found no direct demonstration specific to input-conditioned feature gates. [Siciliano et al. (2024)](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3924/paper1.pdf) demonstrate strong dependence on recent items through missing-suffix experiments; dependence alone does not establish memorization. [PAUDRec (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0957417423019310) documents over-recommendation of popular items in sequential recommendation, while [Prakash et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) show that aggregate accuracy conceals head/mid/tail disparities and that negative-sampling choices affect popularity bias. These motivate controls, rather than prove that a particular gate exploits shortcuts.

Recommended behavioral controls, synthesized from this evidence: freeze one trained NextItNet model; hold candidates, targets, sequence length, padding and the final k items fixed while shuffling earlier items or replacing the prefix with a length- and frequency-matched donor prefix. Sweep k; measure paired HR@10 changes, target-score margins and ranking overlap. Prefix shuffling tests order sensitivity; prefix replacement tests dependence on earlier item content. Separately replace only the last-item anchor with frequency-matched alternatives, then vary anchor frequency while holding the prefix fixed. [Learning Causal Explanations for Recommendation](https://csr21.github.io/xu-csr2021.pdf) provides precedent for length-preserving item replacements. These are model-sensitivity tests, not identified causal effects on user preferences; implausible replacements can create distribution shift.

Define frequency bins from training interactions only; report validation HR@10 and perturbation effects jointly by target frequency, anchor frequency and observed anchor–target transition count, including unseen pairs, with sample counts and uncertainty. Keep the pinned evaluator unchanged; diagnostics supplement category-macro HR@10. Context sensitivity plus validation gains within matched strata supports useful conditioning, without proving absence of memorization. Inspect output changes rather than treating gate weights as explanations; [Jain and Wallace (2019)](https://aclanthology.org/N19-1357/) establish this caution for attention.
